//: Sender identity only. The Resend API key is NEVER read from here: it comes from the
RESEND_API_KEY environment variable and nothing else, so that a credential cannot
arrive from a committed file.
Provider is 'None' by default so a developer can run signup without an account; the
verification email is then written to the log instead of sent. Production sets
Email__Provider=Resend in its environment file, and the host refuses to start if that
is set without a key.
How the portal is reached from outside. Every link Zazi emails — email
verification and password reset — is built from this and never from the
request's Host header, because those links activate accounts and change
passwords, and a URL the caller chooses points wherever they like.
Empty here; production sets Portal__PublicBaseUrl in /etc/zazi/web.env.
Without it, password reset refuses at the page and signup cannot be enabled.
Password reset has no on/off switch: an account holder who has forgotten
their password needs a way back in whether or not the deployment accepts new
signups. It needs Portal:PublicBaseUrl and refuses at the page without it.
ValidForMinutes is deliberately far shorter than email verification's 24
hours — this link changes a password and sits in a mailbox while it lives.
MinimumResponseMilliseconds is a floor on how long a request takes to answer,
so the response time cannot say whether the address had an account.
Self-service signup. Disabled by default: opening a financial system to public
registration is a decision a deployment makes on purpose, not one it inherits.
Requires Portal:PublicBaseUrl when enabled.
